title: Giraffes Can Count Carrots, Scientists Say
summary:
Giraffes are the tallest land animals on Earth. Now scientists say giraffes can also do simple math!

Researchers from the University of Barcelona in Spain tested four giraffes at the Barcelona Zoo. The giraffes love carrots, so the scientists used carrots in the test. The giraffes saw carrots in two yellow boxes. Then they watched the scientists add more carrots to one of the boxes. To get it right, a giraffe had to pick the box with the most carrots.

Two giraffes, Nuru and Njano, picked the right box every time. The other two used shortcuts, such as picking the box the scientist's hand touched last.

The test got harder when carrots were taken away or moved more than once. Then all the giraffes had trouble. Still, the study shows giraffes can keep track of small numbers.

The study was published on June 26, 2026. Scientists think math skills might help wild giraffes find the best food.
why_it_matters: Just like kids comparing snacks, animals may count to choose the best food.
